### RESOLUTION

**OPEN** · goal · JSP-000013

Determine whether every positive t has a real Hadamard matrix of order 4t.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · [YES](#yes), [NO](#no)
- **Evidence** · [github.com](<https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/10e0ab6e7503b6db769029d7d68cc4ca42c011d7/problems/catalog-0001-0100.md#JSP-000013>)

Accept a reviewed proof with a definite polarity. Each child on its own would answer the original question.

### YES

**OPEN** · gate · all positive integers t

There exists H(4t) for every t≥1.

- **Required** · [ODD-REDUCTION](#odd-reduction), [KNOWN-ORDERS](#known-orders), [ALL-D](#all-d)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../README.md](<../README.md>)

The covered odd multipliers are settled, the odd multipliers in D are covered by ALL-D, and doubling handles each remaining even multiplier.

### NO

**OPEN** · gate · one explicit positive integer t

Give t and prove H(4t) does not exist.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · [NO-DESIGN](#no-design), [NO-CLIQUES](#no-cliques)
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

Either an unrestricted design exclusion or a universal exclusion over all pivot pairs at the same t gives the single required counterexample.

### ODD-REDUCTION

**PROVED** · lemma · all positive t

H(n) implies H(2n); every positive t is an odd multiplier times a power of two.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../Constructions.lean](<../Constructions.lean>), [../Reductions.lean](<../Reductions.lean>)

Sylvester doubling and strong induction are proved as double_order and all_of_odd.

### KNOWN-ORDERS

**PUBLISHED** · lemma · odd t outside D

The two direct Paley tests, Scarpis–Đoković orders and t=1,3 supply H(4t) on their stated domains.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../README.md](<../README.md>), [doi.org](<https://doi.org/10.1002/sapm1933121311>), [arxiv.org](<https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00635>)

Use q=4t−1, q=2t−1, or 4t=q(q+1) with the specified prime-power and congruence hypotheses; D is the exact remaining odd domain.

### ALL-D

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

H(4t) exists on the entire remaining domain.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · [BANDS](#bands), [CLIQUE-ROUTE](#clique-route), [DESIGN-ROUTE](#design-route), [TAIL-AND-BASE](#tail-and-base)
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md](<lemmas.md>)

Capacity induction, a uniform clique theorem, the full symmetric design, or a matched tail plus finite proof each suffice on its own. Each route quantifies over the same D.

### SWITCH-FORMULA

**PROVED** · lemma · all k-regular square pairs

The defect energy is nonnegative, vanishes exactly at the required Gram, and its exact two-by-two switch change is known.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#regular-switches](<lemmas.md#regular-switches>)

Each switch preserves regularity; only two rows of off-diagonal column codegrees change. Regular seeds exist for every t.

### FOUR-CYCLE

**PROVED** · lemma · positive defect energy

Positive energy is at least four. At E=4 the defect is one alternating four-cycle; exact one-switch repair is equivalent to a specified row-difference pair.

- **Required** · [SWITCH-FORMULA](#switch-formula)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#regular-switches](<lemmas.md#regular-switches>)

Zero signed degree classifies the support. Substituting the two opposite columns into the switch formula forces the two positive edge sets to be the differences between the chosen rows.

### OUTER

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

Some valid outside design exists at every required order.

- **Required** · [PIVOT](#pivot)
- **Alternatives** · [PAIR-CONSTRUCTION](#pair-construction), [SWITCH-DESCENT](#switch-descent)
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#pivot](<lemmas.md#pivot>)

An explicit Gram pair or a successful two-band descent furnishes the integral block design through PIVOT.

### PAIR-CONSTRUCTION

**OPEN** · obligation · every t in D

Construct a k-regular binary pair with the prescribed column Gram for every t in D.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#pivot](<lemmas.md#pivot>)

A construction on a subfamily contributes exactly its proved coverage; full promotion needs all remaining multipliers.

### SWITCH-DESCENT

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

An energy-zero pair exists at every remaining order by regular switches.

- **Required** · [SWITCH-FORMULA](#switch-formula), [FOUR-CYCLE](#four-cycle), [SWITCH-LOW](#switch-low), [SWITCH-HIGH](#switch-high)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#regular-switches](<lemmas.md#regular-switches>)

Start at the regular circulant seed. Endpoint energies decrease in the positive integers, with the E=4 branch handled separately.

### SWITCH-LOW

**OPEN** · obligation · each attainable E=4 pair, t in D

Prove a finite path of regular switches to zero with intermediate energy at most four, from every energy-four pair.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#regular-switches](<lemmas.md#regular-switches>)

This proposed plateau lemma is sufficient for the low band; the choice of this stronger statement is local to the descent route.

### SWITCH-HIGH

**OPEN** · obligation · each attainable E>4 pair, t in D

Prove a finite path to lower endpoint energy with intermediates at most the starting energy.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#regular-switches](<lemmas.md#regular-switches>)

A switch may be neutral. The proof must establish termination of any neutral phase or construct a finite path directly.

### CAPACITY

**PROVED** · lemma · every admissible prefix and proposed column

The exact local count equations and zero/full deficit boundary bits characterize a fixed-witness append; restricting a terminal prefix gives all smaller widths.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../Rounding.lean](<../Rounding.lean>)

Use appendNext_valid_iff, capacity_appendNext_iff and prefix_of_le. Existential step lemmas may replace the prefix.

### PREFIX-INDUCTION

**PROVED** · lemma · every required integer t

Outer existence plus existential admissible growth at every 0≤j<h implies H(4t).

- **Required** · [ASSEMBLY](#assembly), [LAST-SEVEN](#last-seven)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../Rounding.lean](<../Rounding.lean>), [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

A design starts at width zero. Finite induction, assembly and last-seven completion close the order. from_rounding supplies the corresponding global conditional theorem.

### BANDS

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

All required orders close through the capacity-prefix route.

- **Required** · [OUTER](#outer), [FIRST](#first), [EARLY](#early), [MIDDLE](#middle), [LAST-EIGHT](#last-eight), [PREFIX-INDUCTION](#prefix-induction)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

For a=min(t−1,h−1) the disjoint bands 0, [1,a), [a,h−1), and {h−1} cover all j<h. Induction takes existential outputs, allowing new witnesses.

### FIRST

**OPEN** · gate · j=0 at each t in D

Outer existence implies existence of a capacity-feasible prefix of width one.

- **Required** · [SIGNATURE](#signature), [CAPACITY](#capacity), [COLLISION](#collision)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>), [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

Apply an attainable common signature for a possibly different valid pair. The first chosen bits satisfy capacity automatically.

### COLLISION

**OPEN** · obligation · every t in D

If a valid pair exists at this t, some valid pair A,B admits k-subsets with common degree signature.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>)

A positive histogram overlap proves exactly this first step. A fixed pair with disjoint supports refutes the universal fixed-pair variant only.

### EARLY

**OPEN** · obligation · t in D, 1≤j<a

Existence of an admissible j-prefix implies existence at j+1 in the early band.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

Here j+1≤k, so the capacity box follows automatically. Maintain all inside and mixed intersections on each returned witness.

### MIDDLE

**OPEN** · obligation · t in D, a≤j<h−1

Existence of an admissible j-prefix implies existence at j+1 in the band where capacity can bind.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../Rounding.lean](<../Rounding.lean>), [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

Exact rounding on a suitable prefix with the forced boundary bits suffices. Both Y and the earlier X columns may be replaced.

### KERNEL-EIGHT

**PROVED** · lemma · one n×(n−8) orthogonal sign prefix

Sign extendibility is decidable with at most 128 rational tests; at most 29 independent quadratic coefficient rows suffice.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

Choose independent coordinate rows of the eight-dimensional rational kernel, fix the global sign, and expand each squared row equation in the pair characters.

### LAST-EIGHT

**OPEN** · gate · t in D, j=h−1

Existence of an admissible prefix one before the target implies existence at the target.

- **Required** · [ACCEPT-EIGHT](#accept-eight), [KERNEL-EIGHT](#kernel-eight), [ASSEMBLY](#assembly), [LAST-SEVEN](#last-seven), [EXTRACTION](#extraction)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

Some test-positive prefix supplies n−7 columns. Complete the square and extract the target prefix to recover capacity on one witness.

### ACCEPT-EIGHT

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

Whenever an admissible h−1 prefix exists, some such prefix admits an accepting eight-coordinate sign pattern.

- **Required** · [KERNEL-EIGHT](#kernel-eight), [TERMINAL-TYPES](#terminal-types)
- **Alternatives** · [GOOD-TYPE](#good-type), [GOOD-DIRECT](#good-direct)
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>), [lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight](<lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight>)

A good pattern passes the exact kernel test. A common type factor supplies eight sign columns and in particular one passing pattern. Both alternatives must be uniform in t.

### TERMINAL-TYPES

**PROVED** · lemma · all real sign prefixes with defect eight and n divisible by four

An order-independent finite alphabet of pivot Grams G and row types r determines the exact 128-pattern test, with multiplicity moment Σmᵣrᵀr=nG.

- **Required** · [KERNEL-EIGHT](#kernel-eight)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight](<lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight>)

Take the integral rank-eight matrix nI−CCᵀ and an invertible principal submatrix. Diagonal, parity and positivity bound all entries.

### GOOD-TYPE

**OPEN** · obligation · every t in D admitting an h−1 prefix

Guarantee some h−1 prefix whose realized row types at a single chosen Gram admit a common sign factor S.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight](<lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight>)

The factor simultaneously supports every realized row type. Projector moments and isolated good types are necessary tests only.

### GOOD-DIRECT

**OPEN** · obligation · every t in D admitting an h−1 prefix

Produce some h−1 prefix and one of its 128 patterns satisfying every row test.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction](<lemmas.md#rounding-bands-and-the-last-missing-direction>)

A proof may select a different prefix. The old one need not be extendible.

### CLIQUE-ROUTE

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

Some valid pair with an h-clique is available at every unresolved order.

- **Required** · [CLIQUE-EQUIV](#clique-equiv)
- **Alternatives** · [UNIFORM-CLIQUE](#uniform-clique), [ALGEBRAIC](#algebraic)
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>)

Use the direct selector construction or the algebraic row construction. Each supplies one pair and its whole clique simultaneously.

### UNIFORM-CLIQUE

**OPEN** · obligation · every t in D

Construct or prove existence of some valid A,B and h pairwise adjacent matching selectors at every t in D.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>)

A construction may partition D if the subfamilies have a proved cover. A different pair may serve each multiplier.

### ROW-CONSTRUCTION

**PROVED** · lemma · every t in D

A pair satisfying both Gram identities and AB=BA yields a b-clique and a full square.

- **Required** · [SIGNATURE](#signature), [ASSEMBLY](#assembly)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#a-common-algebraic-construction](<lemmas.md#a-common-algebraic-construction>)

Take (Bᵀeᵢ,Aᵀeᵢ) for each i. The transposed commutation gives signatures and the row Gram gives adjacency.

### ALGEBRAIC

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

Construct full cliques uniformly from commuting representatives with both Gram identities.

- **Required** · [ROW-CONSTRUCTION](#row-construction), [ALGEBRAIC-COVER](#algebraic-cover)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#a-common-algebraic-construction](<lemmas.md#a-common-algebraic-construction>)

The same representative with its chosen row labels must satisfy every identity. Commutative circulant data are a sufficient special case.

### ALGEBRAIC-COVER

**OPEN** · obligation · every t in D

Cover D by explicit constructions of labelled regular pairs satisfying (1) and (3).

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#a-common-algebraic-construction](<lemmas.md#a-common-algebraic-construction>)

A parameterized family and an exact proof of its domain can be accumulated; complete coverage is a separate mathematical requirement.

Prove the block decomposition exists for all remaining t with growing block size 2t−1.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None

### TAIL-AND-BASE

**OPEN** · gate · every t in D

A proved cofinite theorem and verified finite remainder together cover D.

- **Required** · [TAIL](#tail), [FINITE-BASE](#finite-base)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

Use the same explicitly recorded T from TAIL in FINITE-BASE. For any t in D take the appropriate side of t≤T.

### TAIL

**OPEN** · obligation · all t in D above one returned cutoff

Produce a concrete T with proof that H(4t) holds for every t in D greater than T.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

The deliverable is a dependent pair of the value and the tail theorem. Density one or a large finite interval is insufficient.

### FINITE-BASE

**OPEN** · obligation · all t in D up to the exact cutoff from TAIL

For the supplied T, give checked squares or proofs for every t in D with t≤T.

- **Required** · [TAIL](#tail)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

Consume TAIL and bind the manifest to its exact numerical cutoff. Normalize the order convention n=4t.

### NO-DESIGN

**OPEN** · gate · one named t≥2

Exclude the unrestricted full block decomposition at a specific t.

- **Required** · [DESIGN-EQUIV](#design-equiv)
- **Alternatives** · [NO-INVARIANT](#no-invariant), [NO-CERTIFICATE](#no-certificate)
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

A general arithmetic obstruction at that t or a complete checked search for the exact encoding would exclude every square.

### NO-INVARIANT

**OPEN** · obligation · one named positive multiplier t≥2

Prove a contradiction for every full block design at the named multiplier.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

Every extra normalization or group hypothesis must be necessary for all candidate squares or removed.

### NO-CERTIFICATE

**OPEN** · obligation · one named positive multiplier t≥2

Supply a certified UNSAT result for the complete v×v Boolean design encoding at t.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

Use an encoding with both directions proved, then replay a checker-verifiable certificate over all configurations, including any justified symmetry reductions.

### NO-CLIQUES

**OPEN** · gate · one named t in D

At a fixed remaining multiplier, exclude an h-clique for every valid pair.

- **Required** · [CLIQUE-EQUIV](#clique-equiv), [NO-PAIR-COVER](#no-pair-cover)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>)

Use the necessary direction of CLIQUE-EQUIV. The pair space, all selector sets and every symmetry class must be covered.

### NO-PAIR-COVER

**OPEN** · obligation · one named t in D and every admissible A,B at that t

Prove universal exclusion over the pivot-pair space, including the case that no valid pair exists.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>)

One universal obstruction or a complete certificate over all regular-pair cases suffices. A single fixed graph is a proper subset.

### ASSEMBLY

**PROVED** · lemma · all incidence widths

On one row labelling, an outer design and j compatible inner columns give 1+2t+j orthogonal sign columns.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../Assembly.lean](<../Assembly.lean>)

The constant column and the two border signs convert intersection counts to inner products; full width b gives a square directly.

### EXTRACTION

**PROVED** · lemma · all full squares with t≥5

A full normalized H(4t) gives a residual design and every capacity-feasible prefix up to b.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../README.md#the-construction-and-its-converse](<../README.md#the-construction-and-its-converse>)

Normalize row and column signs and count positives. All lower rows have exactly k inner ones in the full square.

### LAST-SEVEN

**PUBLISHED** · lemma · n=4t, t≥5

Any n−7 orthogonal real sign columns of length n can be completed to a square.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [doi.org](<https://doi.org/10.1016/0097-3165(80)90028-X>), [thesis.caltech.edu](<https://thesis.caltech.edu/2899/>)

Apply the published row-completion result after transposition.

### PIVOT

**PROVED** · lemma · every t in D

Outer existence is equivalent to two b×b k-regular binary matrices satisfying AᵀA+BᵀB=tI+(t−2)J.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#pivot](<lemmas.md#pivot>)

Mark one outside point, remove it on one half, complement the other half and invert the construction.

### SIGNATURE

**PROVED** · lemma · one given pivot pair

Valid inner columns are precisely pairs of k-subsets u,v with Aᵀu=Bᵀv.

- **Required** · [PIVOT](#pivot)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>)

The mixed count at the pivot fixes both sizes. The finite-point counts give the signature identity; the first-selector count is the overlap of two signature histograms.

### CLIQUE-EQUIV

**PROVED** · lemma · every t in D

H(4t) iff some unrestricted pivot pair admits a clique of size h.

- **Required** · [SIGNATURE](#signature), [ASSEMBLY](#assembly), [LAST-SEVEN](#last-seven), [EXTRACTION](#extraction)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>)

Adjacency gives exactly the inside codegree t−2. Assemble to n−7 and complete. For the reverse direction normalize a square and use any h inner columns.

### DESIGN-EQUIV

**PROVED** · lemma · every integer t≥2

H(4t) iff the edges of (t−1)K_(4t−1) decompose into copies of K_(2t−1).

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative](<lemmas.md#unrestricted-disproof-and-the-finite-cutoff-alternative>)

Deleting the positive border gives the block design. Conversely pair counting forces the replication and the number of blocks; bordering gives the square.

### FRACTIONAL

**PROVED** · lemma · every admissible prefix j<b

Deficit divided by remaining slots satisfies all next-column equations over the rationals.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../Rounding.lean](<../Rounding.lean>), [../README.md#b--round-the-next-column](<../README.md#b--round-the-next-column>)

Double-count the remaining sizes and intersections. Integral existence remains a separate obligation.

### ODD-CUT

**PROVED** · lemma · odd t≥3

In each equal point partition of an outer design, at most one block can occupy an entire half.

- **Required** · None
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [../OuterEnergy.lean](<../OuterEnergy.lean>), [../README.md#r--choose-the-outside-blocks](<../README.md#r--choose-the-outside-blocks>)

Its imbalance has squared value t², the total is 2t² and all odd imbalances are nonzero. For prime t≥5 this also excludes the two t-cycle symmetry by orbit counting.

### AUGMENTED-KEY

**PROVED** · lemma · one fixed feasible prefix at arbitrary width

Matching augmented signature keys with forced coordinates is equivalent to a legal fixed-witness next column.

- **Required** · [SIGNATURE](#signature), [CAPACITY](#capacity)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#signature](<lemmas.md#signature>), [../Rounding.lean](<../Rounding.lean>)

Append the inner overlaps to the A key and their required complements to the B key, and enforce local capacity boundaries on each half.

### TERMINAL-RANK

**PROVED** · lemma · one defect-eight sign prefix at n=4t, t≥5, for the Verheiden implication

The quadratic tests have rank at most 28; a completable prefix has rank at most 21 and at most 256 distinct projected row types.

- **Required** · [TERMINAL-TYPES](#terminal-types), [LAST-SEVEN](#last-seven)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight](<lemmas.md#finite-row-types-at-defect-eight>)

Use the pivot Gram for one annihilator; completion gives eight independent lifted sign vectors and one common 8×8 sign Gram factor for all realized types.

### EXCHANGE-NINE

**PROVED** · lemma · one fixed n×(n−9) orthogonal sign prefix

At most 256 sign patterns modulo negation enumerate all extending directions. Two orthogonal returned signs yield n−7 columns.

- **Required** · [KERNEL-EIGHT](#kernel-eight)
- **Alternatives** · None
- **Evidence** · [lemmas.md#one-column-replacement](<lemmas.md#one-column-replacement>)

Repeat the eight-dimensional coordinate argument in dimension nine and compare every pair. When applied after deleting one of n−8 columns this exactly tests two-column replacements over that retained prefix.
